title: Normalized geometric model and coefficient square before arithmetic comparison
statement: Fix primes ell and p with p different from ell, a field k of characteristic p, a separable closure ks, a separated finite-type k-scheme X, and a finite intermediate field E in the normed algebraic closure PadicAlgCl(ell). Put A=underline E, C the finite-subextension-valued condensed algebraic closure, and B the all-continuous norm-topological algebraic closure [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Use their internal equivariant module categories and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Supply any normalized invariant functor I, ordinary tensor models TC and TB with trivial action on C and B, universal left-derived tensor pairs LC and LB, and the ordinary tensor transformation eta induced sectionwise by the actual inclusion c:C to B [lem-sfb-profinite-algcl-derived-invariants-comparison]. Let alpha be the universal derived eta followed by ordinary right-derived invariants and point evaluation. For any bounded constructible finite-constant-model V on X [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and the actual pulled-back coefficient inclusion f, there exist a bounded equivariant A-complex K with finite-dimensional continuous E-representation cohomology and, in every integer degree q, isomorphisms from the two cohomology groups of the actual derived global coefficient map to the respective cohomology groups of alpha at K. These isomorphisms intertwine the two maps. The cohomology identifications retain the norm topology, restriction, scalar action and all generalized Galois elements. No invertibility of alpha or of the actual global coefficient map is part of this conclusion.

proof.text: Specialize the normalized geometric finite scalar assertion over ks to an algebraic closure of Q_ell obtained by lifting PadicAlgCl into the scheme universe. Transport its finite subfield E through that lift. On every profinite test set, composing continuous functions with the lift equivalence identifies the finite coefficient sheaf, the finite-subextension-valued coefficient sheaf, and the all-continuous norm coefficient sheaf with the three published coefficient sheaves. The finite-image condition is preserved because the lift bijects finite intermediate subfields. These ring isomorphisms commute with restriction, multiplication and all three scalar inclusions. Exact scalar restriction along them transports geometric sections and their derived scalar extensions, units and projections. The canonical localization equivalence also transports the original scheme-module complex V into the localization universe of the geometric model. Its homology factorization preserves boundedness and finite-constant-model constructibility, and its tensor factorization preserves the actual coefficient maps. Let K be the transported finite-field geometric derived sections. The geometric assertion gives boundedness and finite-dimensional jointly continuous E-representation cohomology in every degree. Its section, scalar and action equations identify those cohomology modules with the corresponding representation models; composing the normalized section identifications identifies any two such models. The zero complex, empty scheme and zero-dimensional representations are covered by the same construction.

proof.text: Compare the specified ordinary tensor models with restriction of equivariant scalar extension. Their underlying tensor identifications and generalized-action formulas give an equivariant natural isomorphism with the normalized relative tensor functors. One checks action compatibility on pure tensors after every profinite base change and then uses the sheafified tensor universal property. The section equations for c and eta identify the ordinary transformation with the actual coefficient inclusion. Derive these identifications by the universal left-derived counits; counit-compatible uniqueness identifies both derived tensor functors and their natural transformation. For scalar extension followed by exact scalar restriction, this is the same derived pair by the K-flat construction of relative tensor. The unit equations fix the geometric projection and coefficient morphisms under these identifications.

proof.text: The supplied invariant functor and the geometric invariant functor are both the normalized right adjoint to trivial action. Right-adjoint uniqueness identifies them compatibly with their inclusions of fixed sections. The analogous point-evaluation and finite-coefficient-forgetting identifications preserve ordinary right-derived functors: normalized injective or K-injective resolutions and the derived universal property give the comparison. In particular, coefficient forgetting preserves K-injectives: its free-coefficient left adjoint is exact since the finite coefficient sheaf is sectionwise a rational vector space and is therefore flat over the constant integers. The normalized internal/section-module equivalence identifies the tensors used in this statement. Exactness of forgetting alone is not used as a substitute for this adjoint argument. Finite type over Spec(k) makes X quasi-compact, and separatedness makes it quasi-separated. Thus the compactness and quasi-separatedness hypotheses for descent hold. Apply ordinary condensed Galois descent to both coefficient extensions of V. Compose descent with the two invertible geometric projections. Their naturality for the actual scalar inclusion and the geometric coefficient square give a commuting square whose bottom edge is the prescribed alpha at K. The top edge is the original explicit single-tensor coefficient map, since both are fixed by the scalar adjunction unit and send z tensor v to c(z) tensor v.

proof.text: The geometric descent square is initially expressed in a larger localization universe. Both localizations invert the same quasi-isomorphisms; their canonical comparison identifies their homology functors since both factor the ordinary complex homology functor. Apply each homology functor to the preceding square. This yields the endpoint isomorphisms eC and eB and the displayed equation in the common category of abelian groups, independent of the chosen localization universe. This step asserts no invertibility for alpha and uses no arithmetic cohomological dimension bound.

theorem geometric_comparison_normalization
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (hpℓ : p ≠ ℓ)
    (a : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType a] [QuasiCompact a] [IsSeparated a]
    [ActionAbelian (scalarRing.{u} ℓ E) (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks)]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u + 1} (Equivariant (scalarRing.{u} ℓ E) (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2} (Equivariant (scalarRing.{u} ℓ E) (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2} Ab.{u + 1}]
    (I : Invariants (scalarRing.{u} ℓ E) (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks))
    [(pointEvaluation.{u} ℓ E).Additive]
    (TC : TensorModel ℓ E (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks) (finiteModule ℓ E))
    (TB : TensorModel ℓ E (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks) (normModule ℓ E))
    (c : finiteModule.{u} ℓ E ⟶ normModule ℓ E)
    (eta : TC.functor ⟶ TB.functor)
    (LC : DerivedTensor ℓ E (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks) TC)
    (LB : DerivedTensor ℓ E (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks) TB)
    (hc : ∀ (S : Profinite.{u}) (z : (finiteModule ℓ E).X.obj.obj (op S)),
      ((c.hom.hom.app (op S)) z).down = z.down.val)
    (heta : ∀ M : Equivariant (scalarRing ℓ E) (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks),
      (eta.app M).val ≫ TB.underlying.hom.app M =
        TC.underlying.hom.app M ≫ c ▷ M.module)
    (V : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X)))
    (hV : constantModelBoundedConstructible (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X V) :
    let alpha := Functor.whiskerRight (derivedCoefficientMap ℓ E (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks) LC LB eta)
      (I.functor ⋙ pointEvaluation ℓ E).rightDerivedFunctor
    let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{u + 1}
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} Ab.{u + 1} :=
      HasDerivedCategory.ofIsGrothendieckAbelian Ab.{u + 1}
    ∃ K : DerivedCategory (Equivariant (scalarRing.{u} ℓ E) (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks)),
      DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.bounded K ∧
      (∀ q : ℤ, ∃ (W : Type (u + 1)) (ng : NormedAddCommGroup W),
        letI := ng
        ∃ (ns : NormedSpace E W), letI := ns
        ∃ (fd : FiniteDimensional E W) (rho : (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks) →* Module.End E W),
          Continuous (fun x : (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks) × W ↦ rho x.1 x.2) ∧
          ∃ N : RepresentationModel ℓ E (ks ≃ₐ[k] ks) W rho,
            Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K ≅ N.object)) ∧
      ∃ (eC : ∀ q : ℤ,
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{u + 1} q).obj ((derivedGlobalSections ℓ X E).obj
            (Arrow.mk (comparison ℓ X E V)).left) ≅
            (H q).obj (Arrow.mk (alpha.app K)).left)
        (eB : ∀ q : ℤ,
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{u + 1} q).obj ((derivedGlobalSections ℓ X E).obj
            (Arrow.mk (comparison ℓ X E V)).right) ≅
            (H q).obj (Arrow.mk (alpha.app K)).right),
        ∀ q : ℤ, (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{u + 1} q).map
          ((derivedGlobalSections ℓ X E).map
            (comparison ℓ X E V)) ≫
            (eB q).hom = (eC q).hom ≫ (H q).map (alpha.app K)
